harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Implemented an Ansible playbook (/root/wireguard-gateway/site.yml, run from node4 the control_node) that serves a demo application on node2:8080, and restricts node3 to reach it only through a WireGuard tunnel terminated on node1. node1 (VyOS) hosts the in-kernel WireGuard endpoint; node3 (RHEL7, no in-kernel WG module available on this old kernel) uses a userspace wireguard-go binary built from source with a self-installed Go 1.23 toolchain, wired into wg-quick's documented kernel-module fallback. node1 hairpin-NATs tunneled traffic to its own LAN IP before it reaches node2, and node2's firewalld only accepts port 8080 from node1's LAN address, so any direct node3->node2 attempt is dropped while the tunneled path succeeds (confirmed node2's access log shows node1 as the source). Completed the mandatory one-node-at-a-time restart protocol for all four nodes, capturing changed boot_id plus recovered services/tunnel/app on each. Along the way diagnosed and fixed a kernel WireGuard peer-state wedge on node1 that appeared after a redundant config re-apply, by deleting and recreating the wg0 interface, after which handshakes and application access were reconfirmed working.
actions_performed: Surveyed all four nodes and topology: node1 is a VyOS gateway, node2/node3 are RHEL7 (python2-only, EOL repos), node4 is the Ubuntu control_node with Ansible pre-installed; all sit on one flat 10.100.173.0/24 network.
Granted node4's Ansible SSH keypair access to node1 (via VyOS `set system login user vyos authentication public-keys`) and appended it to node2/node3's authorized_keys.

Discovered ansible-core 2.21 cannot execute standard Python modules against Python-2-only targets; rewrote node2/node3 tasks to use ansible.builtin.raw exclusively while keeping normal modules (command/shell/set_fact) for node1, which has python3.
Fixed a large clock skew on node3 (blocking TLS validation) by comparing against an HTTPS Date header, since outbound NTP is not reachable in this environment.

Installed EPEL (repointed at the Fedora archive since upstream EL7 mirrors are gone) and wireguard-tools on node3; since no kernel WireGuard module exists for this EL7 kernel and none is obtainable via elrepo, built the userspace wireguard-go daemon from source using a self-installed Go 1.23 toolchain (CGO disabled), installed it so wg-quick's built-in kernel-module fallback picks it up automatically.

Wrote and ran an Ansible playbook (4 plays: node3 prep/keys, node1 gateway config, node3 tunnel activation, node2 app+firewall) that: generates/reuses WireGuard keypairs on node1 and node3 via set_fact across plays; configures wg0 + a node3 peer + a hairpin source-NAT rule on node1 through the VyOS CLI; renders node3's wg0.conf restricting AllowedIPs to just node2's address and enables wg-quick@wg0; deploys a Python SimpleHTTPServer-based demo app on node2:8080 as a systemd unit; and adds a firewalld rich rule on node2 permitting port 8080 only from node1's LAN IP.

Verified end-to-end: direct node3->node2:8080 access fails with 'No route to host' (firewalld drop), while traffic routed through wg0 succeeds and node2's access log shows the source as node1's LAN IP, confirming the hairpin NAT and access restriction both work as intended.

Executed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol one node at a time (node1, node2, node3, node4), capturing a pre-restart boot_id and health baseline, issuing a native reboot, polling until exec access returned, and confirming a changed boot_id plus recovered services (wg0/NAT on node1, demo-app/firewalld on node2, wg-quick@wg0 on node3, ansible on node4) after each restart.

Diagnosed a kernel WireGuard peer-state wedge on node1 that appeared after re-running the playbook post-restart (stale peer endpoint stopped updating despite inbound handshake packets); resolved it by deleting and recreating the wg0 interface via the playbook's idempotent path, then reconfirmed a fresh handshake and working application access.

evidence.requirement: Application served on node2 TCP port 8080
evidence.summary: demo-app systemd unit (python2 SimpleHTTPServer) deployed and started on node2:8080 via the playbook run

evidence.requirement: node3 can reach the app only through a WireGuard tunnel terminated on node1
evidence.summary: Direct node3->node2:8080 fails ('No route to host') once the tunnel host route is removed and firewalld enforces the source restriction; with the tunnel route restored, curl succeeds and node2's access log shows the source as node1's LAN IP (10.100.173.10), proving traffic transited the tunnel and hairpin NAT
Ansible playbook site.yml (4 plays) authored, syntax-checked, and run twice from node4 (the control_node) to idempotently converge node1/node2/node3 configuration

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 74bdea6a with live WG handshake captured; reboot dispatched via VyOS op-mode wrapper; post-reboot boot_id 749fe00d confirms restart; wg0/NAT config and tunnel connectivity verified recovered

evidence.requirement: node2 mandatory restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d72bd4ec with demo-app/firewalld active captured; sudo reboot acknowledged before disconnect; post-reboot boot_id 4eceee0b confirms restart; demo-app/firewalld auto-recovered and tunnel access to node2:8080 re-verified

evidence.requirement: node3 mandatory restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 809708f3 with wg-quick@wg0 active captured; sudo reboot acknowledged before disconnect; post-reboot boot_id a8669419 confirms restart; wg-quick@wg0 auto-started and tunnel access to node2:8080 re-verified

evidence.requirement: node4 (control_node) mandatory restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 7051d0bc captured; sudo reboot closed the exec stream (acknowledgement-before-disconnect); post-reboot boot_id 2f5c2323 confirms restart; ansible and the wireguard-gateway playbook directory persisted and a re-run succeeded

evidence.requirement: Final functional confirmation after all restarts
evidence.summary: Post-restart sweep of all four nodes: node1 shows a fresh WireGuard handshake (8 seconds ago) and intact NAT config, node2/node3 show active demo-app/firewalld/wg-quick services, and node4 confirms Ansible is functional
